column1: More than two hundred years ago, Russian explorers and fur hunters landed on the Aleutian Islands, a volcanic archipelago in the North Pacific, and learned of a land mass that lay farther to the north.
column2: 两百多年前，俄国探险家和毛皮猎人登上了阿留申群岛，那是北太平洋的一组火山岛。他们还得知更北边有一片陆地。

column1: The islands’ native inhabitants called this land mass Aleyska, the ‘Great Land’; today, we know it as Alaska.
column2: 岛上的原住民称这片陆地为Aleyska，意为“伟大的土地”；今天我们称它为阿拉斯加。

column1: The forty-ninth state to join the United States of America (in 1959), Alaska is fully one-fifth the size of the mainland 48 states combined.
column2: 作为第49个加入美国的州（1959年），阿拉斯加的面积为全美48个州总面积的五分之一。

column1: It shares, with Canada, the second longest river system in North America and has over half the coastline of the United States.
column2: 它与加拿大共同拥有北美洲第二长的河流系统，其海岸线长度也超过了美国的一半。

column1: The rivers feed into the Bering Sea and Gulf of Alaska - cold, nutrient-rich waters which support tens of millions of seabirds, and over 400 species of fish, shellfish, crustaceans, and molluscs.
column2: 这些河流注入白令海和阿拉斯加湾。那里寒冷而富含养分的水域，养育着数千万只海鸟，以及四百多种鱼类、贝类、甲壳类和软体动物。
column5: Gulf of Alaska|n. 阿拉斯加湾
column9: tens of millions of|数以千万计的

column1: Taking advantage of this rich bounty, Alaska’s commercial fisheries have developed into some of the largest in the world.
column2: 利用这一丰富的资源，阿拉斯加的商业渔业已经发展成为全球规模最大的渔业之一。

column1: According to the Alaska Department of Fish and Game (ADF&G), Alaska’s commercial fisheries landed hundreds of thousands of tonnes of shellfish and herring, and well over a million tonnes of groundfish (cod, sole, perch and pollock) in 2000.
column2: 据阿拉斯加州渔猎局（ADF&G）统计，2000年阿拉斯加商业渔业捕获上岸的贝类和鲱鱼达数十万吨，底层鱼类（鳕鱼、鳎鱼、鲈鱼和狭鳕）的捕获量则远超一百万吨。
column6: hundreds of thousands of|数十万的

column1: The true cultural heart and soul of Alaska’s fisheries, however, is salmon.
column2: 然而，阿拉斯加渔业真正的文化核心与精神所在是鲑鱼。

column1: ‘Salmon,’ notes writer Susan Ewing in The Great Alaska Nature Factbook, ‘pump through Alaska like blood through a heart, bringing rhythmic, circulating nourishment to land, animals and people.’
column2: 作家苏珊·尤因在《阿拉斯加自然知识大全》中写道：“鲑鱼游遍阿拉斯加，犹如血液流经心脏，给这片土地、这里的动物和人带来循环往复、富有节律的滋养。”

column1: The ‘predictable abundance of salmon allowed some native cultures to flourish,’ and ‘dying spawners feed bears, eagles, other animals, and ultimately the soil itself.’
column2: 鲑鱼“总会如期大量出现，使一些原住民文化得以繁荣”，而“产卵后濒死的鲑鱼滋养着熊、鹰和其他动物，最终还滋养了土壤本身”。
column3: predictable abundance|可以预期的大量出现

column1: All five species of Pacific salmon - chinook, or king; chum, or dog; coho, or silver; sockeye, or red; and pink, or humpback - spawn in Alaskan waters, and 90% of all Pacific salmon commercially caught in North America are produced there.
column2: 五种太平洋鲑鱼，包括帝王鲑（又称王鲑）、大麻哈鱼（又称狗鲑）、银鲑、红鲑和粉红鲑（又称驼背鲑），都在阿拉斯加水域产卵。北美商业捕捞的太平洋鲑鱼中，有90%产自那里。
column4: chinook, or king|n. 帝王鲑，又称王鲑
column5: chum, or dog|n. 大麻哈鱼，又称狗鲑
column8: pink, or humpback|n. 粉红鲑，又称驼背鲑

column1: Indeed, if Alaska was an independent nation, it would be the largest producer of wild salmon in the world.
column2: 事实上，如果阿拉斯加成为一个独立的国家，它将成为全球野生鲑鱼产量最大的国家。

column1: During 2000, commercial catches of Pacific salmon in Alaska exceeded 320,000 tonnes, with an ex-vessel value of over $US260 million.
column2: 2000年，阿拉斯加太平洋鲑鱼的商业捕捞量超过32万吨，离岸价值超过2.6亿美元。

column1: Catches have not always been so healthy.
column2: 过去，渔获量并不总是如此可观。

column1: Between 1940 and 1959, overfishing led to crashes in salmon populations so severe that in 1953 Alaska was declared a federal disaster area.
column2: 1940年至1959年间，过度捕捞导致鲑鱼种群数量锐减，情况极其严重，以至于1953年阿拉斯加被宣布为联邦灾区。

column1: With the onset of statehood, however, the State of Alaska took over management of its own fisheries, guided by a state constitution which mandates that Alaska’s natural resources be managed on a sustainable basis.
column2: 不过，阿拉斯加成为美国的一个州后，接管了本州的渔业管理。州政府依照州宪法办事，宪法规定阿拉斯加的自然资源必须以可持续的方式管理。
column4: statehood|n. 成为美国一州的地位
column12: on a sustainable basis|以可持续的方式

column1: At that time, statewide harvests totalled around 25 million salmon.
column2: 当时，全州的鲑鱼捕捞量总计约为2500万条。

column1: Over the next few decades average catches steadily increased as a result of this policy of sustainable management, until, during the 1990s, annual harvests were well in excess of 100 million, and on several occasions over 200 million fish.
column2: 在随后的几十年里，这一可持续管理政策使平均捕捞量稳步上升。到20世纪90年代，每年的捕捞量已远超一亿条，有好几年还超过了两亿条。
column3: Over the next few decades|在随后的几十年里

column1: The primary reason for such increases is what is known as ‘In-Season Abundance-Based Management’.
column2: 此类增长的主要原因被称为‘基于当季丰度的管理’。

column1: There are biologists throughout the state constantly monitoring adult fish as they show up to spawn.
column2: 在该州各地，都有生物学家不断监测那些即将进行繁殖的成年鱼类。

column1: The biologists sit in streamside counting towers, study sonar, watch from aeroplanes, and talk to fishermen.
column2: 那些生物学家们坐在溪流旁的观测塔中，使用声呐设备进行研究，从飞机上观察周围环境，同时与渔民们进行交流。

column1: The salmon season in Alaska is not pre-set.
column2: 阿拉斯加的鲑鱼捕捞季节并不是固定的。

column1: The fishermen know the approximate time of year when they will be allowed to fish, but on any given day, one or more field biologists in a particular area can put a halt to fishing.
column2: 渔民知道每年大致什么时候可以捕鱼，但在任何一天，某个地区的一名或多名野外生物学家都可以叫停当地的捕捞活动。
column6: on any given day|在任何一天
column10: put a halt to|叫停；使停止

column1: Even sport fishing can be brought to a halt.
column2: 就连运动钓鱼这项活动也可能被迫停止。

column1: It is this management mechanism that has allowed Alaska salmon stocks - and, accordingly, Alaska salmon fisheries - to prosper, even as salmon populations in the rest of the United States are increasingly considered threatened or even endangered.
column2: 正是这种管理机制使阿拉斯加的鲑鱼资源得以兴旺，也因此使当地鲑鱼渔业得以繁荣。与此同时，在美国其他地区，鲑鱼种群却日益被视为受到威胁，甚至濒临灭绝。
column8: even as|conj. 尽管与此同时

column1: In 1999, the Marine Stewardship Council (MSC) commissioned a review of the Alaska salmon fishery.
column2: 1999年，海洋管理委员会（Marine Stewardship Council, MSC）委托对阿拉斯加鲑鱼渔业进行了审查。

column1: The Council, which was founded in 1996, certifies fisheries that meet high environmental standards, enabling them to use a label that recognises their environmental responsibility.
column2: 该委员会成立于1996年，负责认证那些符合高标准环保要求的渔业，这些渔业因此可以获得一个体现其环境责任的标签。

column1: The MSC has established a set of criteria by which commercial fisheries can be judged.
column2: MSC已制定一套标准，用于评判商业渔业。

column1: Recognising the potential benefits of being identified as environmentally responsible, fisheries approach the Council requesting to undergo the certification process.
column2: 渔业部门认识到被认定为环保型企业的潜在好处，因此向理事会申请开展认证流程。

column1: The MSC then appoints a certification committee, composed of a panel of fisheries experts, which gathers information and opinions from fishermen, biologists, government officials, industry representatives, non-governmental organisations and others.
column2: 随后，海洋管理委员会任命一个由渔业专家组成的认证委员会。该委员会向渔民、生物学家、政府官员、行业代表、非政府组织及其他各方收集信息和意见。

column1: Some observers thought the Alaska salmon fisheries would not have any chance of certification when, in the months leading up to MSC’s final decision, salmon runs throughout western Alaska completely collapsed.
column2: 一些观察人士当时认为，阿拉斯加鲑鱼渔业根本没有获得认证的机会：在海洋管理委员会作出最终决定前的几个月里，整个阿拉斯加西部的鲑鱼洄游数量骤减。
column5: would not have any chance of|根本没有……的机会
column7: in the months leading up to|在……之前的几个月里
column9: salmon runs|鲑鱼洄游；洄游鱼群
column12: completely collapsed|彻底崩溃；数量锐减

column1: In the Yukon and Kuskokwim rivers, chinook and chum runs were probably the poorest since statehood; subsistence communities throughout the region, who normally have priority over commercial fishing, were devastated.
column2: 在育空河和库斯科奎姆河，帝王鲑和狗鲑的洄游数量很可能是阿拉斯加建州以来最少的。整个地区依靠捕鱼维生的社区都遭受了沉重打击，而这些社区捕鱼通常享有优先于商业捕捞的权利。
column9: subsistence communities|依靠当地资源维生的社区
column12: have priority over|比……享有优先权

column1: The crisis was completely unexpected, but researchers believe it had nothing to do with impacts of fisheries.
column2: 这场危机完全出乎意料，但研究人员认为，这与渔业活动的影响无关。

column1: Rather, they contend, it was almost certainly the result of climatic shifts, prompted in part by cumulative effects of the el niño / la niña phenomenon on Pacific Ocean temperatures, culminating in a harsh winter in which huge numbers of salmon eggs were frozen.
column2: 他们认为，这几乎可以肯定是气候变化所致。厄尔尼诺和拉尼娜现象对太平洋水温的累积影响，是引发这种气候变化的部分原因；最终出现了一个严冬，大量鲑鱼卵被冻住。
column6: prompted in part by|部分由……引起

column1: It could have meant the end as far as the certification process was concerned.
column2: 就认证流程而言，这很可能意味着一切的终结。

column1: However, the state reacted quickly, closing down all fisheries, even those necessary for subsistence purposes.
column2: 然而，政府迅速采取了行动，关闭了所有渔业场所，甚至包括那些用于维持生计的渔业活动。

column1: In September 2000, MSC announced that the Alaska salmon fisheries qualified for certification.
column2: 2000年9月，MSC宣布阿拉斯加鲑鱼渔业符合认证标准。

column1: Seven companies producing Alaska salmon were immediately granted permission to display the MSC logo on their products.
column2: 有七家生产阿拉斯加鲑鱼的公司获得了在产品上使用MSC标志的许可。

column1: Certification is for an initial period of five years, with an annual review to ensure that the fishery is continuing to meet the required standards.
column2: 该认证的有效期为五年，期间会进行年度审核，以确保该渔业持续符合相关标准。
